reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an informational promotion for a Google IT Support certificate through Coursera, including course duration, workload, enrollment, and preparation for entry-level jobs. The seven-day trial, later payment, cancellation option, and sign-up fields are described as ordinary course-access details. Although the employment language is broad, the narration focuses on completing the course, receiving a certificate, updating a resume, and applying for jobs rather than purchasing a guaranteed job.

citations.quote: The tech giant is offering IT support professional certificate course. Through the online education portal Coursera. And you can enroll in the program right away.
The duration of the program is 8 months.
The whole program includes a total of 6 courses
you will have the. Freedom to enjoy a seven-day free trial after which the student will have to pay rupees 3153.
If you think the course is not right. For you, you can simply cancel before the trial ends.

opening.argument: The central pitch links an unusually accessible employment outcome to an immediate enrollment action. The title presents “150,000+ Vacancies,” while the narration says viewers can “get a job at Google” and immediately enroll in the course. That makes the course registration the practical gateway to the promised reward: a Google job. The pathway is reinforced by instructions to visit Coursera and use its enrollment process, followed by a stated payment after the trial. Even if a certificate may exist, the persuasive structure encourages viewers to act on the employment promise before they have any assurance that completing the course produces a job.

citations.quote: Work at Google with 150,000+ Vacancies
Now even you can get a job at Google.
And you can enroll in the program right away.
after which the student will have to pay rupees 3153.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this ordinary course information, but that does not answer the employment solicitation. Its own cited details establish a paid enrollment funnel; they do not establish that the prominent Google-job framing is limited to education rather than used to motivate registration. Describing cancellation after a trial also does not remove the concern that viewers are first drawn in by the promise of access to a highly desirable job.

citations.quote: Work at Google with 150,000+ Vacancies
Now even you can get a job at Google.
you will have the. Freedom to enjoy a seven-day free trial

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The employment language is aspirational, but the quoted action is enrollment in a course, not payment for a job or a promise of guaranteed hiring. The narration expressly says the course prepares students for entry-level jobs and instructs them to update a resume and apply for jobs after earning the certificate. The trial, payment, and cancellation terms are disclosed rather than concealed.

citations.quote: The program will boost employment as it will prepare. Students for the entry-level IT jobs
Upon successfully completing the course,. You will get a complete certificate. Update your resume and apply for jobs.
If you think the course is not right. For you, you can simply cancel before the trial ends.

opening.argument: Several genuine risk signals appear together: a headline promising work at Google and “150,000+ Vacancies,” a claim that anyone can enroll without eligibility or prior experience, and a direct route into a paid subscription. The narration says “Anyone can enroll” and that there are “no eligibility criteria,” then explains that payment follows a seven-day trial. The visual material also shows a Coursera sign-up form requesting a full name, email, and password, alongside a $49/month price graphic. This combination makes the offer look exceptionally easy and urgent while tying access to account creation and payment, a pattern that can mislead viewers about how readily the advertised employment outcome follows.

citations.quote: Work at Google with 150,000+ Vacancies
Anyone can enroll himself or herself for it. There is no. Boundary at all.
There are no eligibility criteria and you need not have prior. Working experience at all.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes duration and course structure, but those details can coexist with deceptive framing. It does not explain why the headline foregrounds a massive vacancy figure or why viewers are told they can get a Google job immediately. Nor does a disclosed trial eliminate the risk signal created by collecting account details and then converting access into a recurring monthly charge.

citations.quote: Work at Google with 150,000+ Vacancies
Now even you can get a job at Google.
after which the student will have to pay rupees 3153.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals describe a low-barrier online course, not a low-barrier cash or asset acquisition scheme. The course page visibly identifies the Google IT Support Professional Certificate and provides workload and course information. Payment is presented as a condition after a seven-day trial, with cancellation available before the trial ends, while the promised employment is framed as preparation for jobs rather than automatic hiring.

citations.quote: The duration of the program is 8 months.
you can simply cancel before the trial ends.
The program will boost employment as it will prepare. Students for the entry-level IT jobs

opening.argument: Although presented as helpful career information, the video functions as a promotional funnel. It opens with the attention-grabbing claim of Google employment, tells viewers to enroll immediately, gives a specific Coursera URL, and separately asks viewers to subscribe. The description explicitly says to “Apply for Google IT Course on Coursera,” while the visuals show an enrollment button and account sign-up interface. These are participation-driving instructions, not merely neutral reporting. The educational framing therefore softens a solicitation for a paid course by surrounding it with Google branding and an employment narrative.

citations.quote: Work at Google with 150,000+ Vacancies
Apply for Google IT Course on Coursera: http://www.coursera.org/specializations/google-it-support.
And you can enroll in the program right away.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a certificate course does not make the presentation neutral. The description gives a direct application URL, and the narration pairs the Google-job claim with immediate enrollment. The defense lists ordinary course features but does not address the promotional choice to lead with employment at Google or the visible sign-up pathway that turns the video into an acquisition message.

citations.quote: Apply for Google IT Course on Coursera: http://www.coursera.org/specializations/google-it-support.
Now even you can get a job at Google.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a real paid educational service is not by itself a scam. The description identifies Coursera and supplies the course link, while the narration explains the six-course structure, projects, certificate, workload, trial, and cancellation. Those disclosures give viewers information needed to evaluate the purchase; they do not show that the video claims enrollment guarantees employment.
